introduction: On this third Sunday of Easter, the apostles, though forbidden to preach, declare that they must obey God rather than men. In the Gospel, the risen Jesus appears by the Sea of Tiberias, gives the disciples a great catch of fish, shares breakfast with them, and asks Peter three times, Do you love me? In heaven, countless angels sing to the Lamb who was slain. Let us answer the Lord's question with love.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the risen Lord feeds us and calls us to follow him. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Pope and the shepherds of the Church: that, like Peter, they may love Christ and feed his sheep. Let us pray to the Lord.
For Christians who are forbidden to speak of their faith: that they may obey God with courage and joy. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who have failed or denied the Lord: that they may hear his call to love him again. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who work all night and catch nothing: that the Lord may bless their labor. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may answer the question of Jesus, Do you love me, with our whole lives. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God of life, your risen Son shared bread with his disciples and restored Peter with love. Help us to love him above all, and to care for those he entrusts to us. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Do you love me?
reflection.body:
After the Resurrection, some of the disciples go back to Galilee. Peter says simply, "I'm going fishing," and the others go with him. They fish all night and catch nothing. At dawn, a man on the shore tells them to cast the net on the right side of the boat, and they cannot haul it in for the number of fish. The beloved disciple recognizes him first: "It's the Lord!" Peter jumps into the sea to reach him.

On the shore Jesus has a fire going, with fish and bread. He says, "Come and eat breakfast!" He takes the bread and gives it to them, as he did at the Last Supper. The risen Lord meets his friends in the ordinary things of life: work, failure, a shared meal.

Then comes a moment between Jesus and Peter. Peter had denied Jesus three times beside a charcoal fire. Now, beside another fire, Jesus asks him three times: "Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me?" Peter is hurt by the third question, but he answers, "Lord, you know everything. You know that I have affection for you." Each time, Jesus gives him a mission: "Feed my lambs... Tend my sheep... Feed my sheep." Peter's failure is healed, and his love is turned into service. Then Jesus says, "Follow me."

In the first reading, Peter is no longer afraid. Ordered to stop preaching, he and the apostles answer, "We must obey God rather than men." After being flogged, they leave "rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer dishonor for Jesus' name."

Jesus asks each of us the same question. This week, let him ask you: Do you love me? Answer him honestly in prayer. Then ask him whom he wants you to feed and care for.
